correctness.rationale: For positive p,q and admissible x0,a, Y=(p+qx)/(1-x) conjugates Bass flow to exponential scaling. The exact positive-denominator P_a(Y) formula, a flow-variation derivative whose sign increases from negative to positive at most once, an exact endpoint Möbius subtraction, and a direct strictly positive H_c-H_* identity prove all continuous-time and cap boundary quantifiers. The proportional-remaining reach derivative is strictly negative. Replay of verify.py passes 220,577 exact-rational assertions, including the exact switch example, but is not substituted for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The proposed complete one-impulse horizon and saturation classification is not a statement of the original Bass equation, continuous-advertising profit optimization, discrete initial-seeding allocation, stochastic rate-phase sorting, or two-rate attrition-flow ordering. Material primary equations and control domains were compared, not merely titles. Priority remains provisional against uninspected general hybrid-control and older product-sampling literature.
residual_risks: The 1995 Jain/Mahajan/Muller product sampling paper was checked at abstract level only; it focuses on optimal number of samples at launch, but uninspected full text could contain a related impulse result.
Delre et al. (2007) was accessible at abstract level only; no global claim about its full text is made.
General hybrid impulsive-control / scalar Riccati projective-flow optimization theory might imply the whole theorem in abstract language; its full corpus was not exhaustively inspected.
Prior math or marketing results not indexed under Bass, giveaway, or seeding terminology could be equivalent; no priority certification.

value.rationale: A mathematically complete one-intervention timing phase diagram in a standard consumer-adoption model: explicit threshold for an actual first-to-last switch, exact non-saturated equality set, explicit late saturation plateau, and exact contrasting always-early law for fixed proportional remaining-market reach. It distinguishes natural but economically nonequivalent notions of a promotion fixed reach without claiming downstream empirical or profitability effects; relevant literature on seeding and advertising shows a motivated gap.
